sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 16 = check #15; Internal Quality Checks row 16; Deterministic Checks rows on check-dockerfiles.py, check-assets-referenced.py, check-package-manifest-deps-preinstalled.py, check-runtime-deps-in-both-images.py)
evidence: Every item of the skill's verification list (quality-checks.md:67) holds in task/environment/Dockerfile. Pinned base: line 1 `FROM node:22-bookworm-slim`. Runtime dependencies pre-installed globally with exact versions: lines 9-12 `npm install -g --no-audit --no-fund express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1`, matching line 3 `ENV NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules`. Assets staged: line 14 `COPY instructions/ /instructions/`, line 15 `COPY assets/ /assets/`, line 16 `chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets`. /app created, git-initialised and empty apart from .gitkeep: lines 17-23. No COPY of solution/ or tests/. The file is byte-identical to the frozen template environment/Dockerfile (diff empty; sha256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1), and tests/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template too, carrying the same express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (lines 20-21) with the same NODE_PATH (line 9). task.toml sets no [environment].docker_image, so the Dockerfile is what builds. The declared world matches the brief: integration.md:5 says `The launch image supplies Node 22, Express and better-sqlite3 through NODE_PATH` and forbids an install or build step at open time; instruction.md:3 and integration.md:7 name /assets/seed_data.json, which exists (149 bytes, parses, keys snippets and note) and is copied. No run-time install anywhere: grep for npm, npx, apt-get, pip, curl and wget in tests/test.sh and solution/solve.sh returns nothing; solve.sh:38-39 only removes the database files and runs `cp -a`. The golden needs nothing beyond the image: server.js:2-5 requires only node:path, node:fs, express and better-sqlite3; the other package.json dependencies (react, react-dom, prettier, acorn, acorn-walk, @lezer/html) are frontend code already bundled into the committed public/assets/index.js and index.css, served by express.static (server.js:130); the bundle contains no off-origin resource load (only namespace and documentation URL strings). Conforming alternative: an agent that vendors its own packages under /app/node_modules is allowed by integration.md:11 and needs no image support; network is public during the build phase, so build tools can be fetched by the agent, which the deterministic sheet treats as a NOTE, not a defect. Broken-app probe: an app that depends on a server package absent from the image and not vendored fails at launch, which is the intended outcome of the stated contract, not a harness fault. Things I did not measure: I ran no docker build in this review (Docker was excluded from my assignment). The raw evidence index records a scripted golden run on these task bytes in an agent image, with solve.sh install and a test.sh-style launch (env -i, uid 65534, NODE_PATH, DB_PATH); I verified the sha256 of run_golden.sh, results/runtime.json and results/restart.json against the index and they match. That run uses a pre-built image tag (run_golden.sh:14 `cw-editor-agent-r3`), which is not hash-bound to this Dockerfile, so it supports but does not prove a fresh build of these bytes; the hosted Oracle run was on an earlier candidate. Minor observations that are not defects under this rubric: the base is pinned by tag, not digest, and apt packages (line 5-6) are unversioned, which the Deterministic Checks sheet classes as a NOTE for check-dockerfiles.py; both are template-controlled lines that the workspace rules say to preserve.
